sections.skill: Read false positives and false negatives and decide which matters more

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: What is a false positive?

choices.text: A wrong "no," where the tool missed something that it should have flagged as a yes

questions.intro: When a tool says YES or NO, such as "spam" or "not spam," it can be wrong in two ways. A FALSE POSITIVE is a wrong YES: a real email marked as spam. A FALSE NEGATIVE is a wrong NO: a spam email let through. A table of results shows both. Which mistake matters more DEPENDS ON THE SITUATION. For spam, a false positive may hide an important message. For a smoke detector, a false negative, missing a real fire, is far worse than a false alarm. Often reducing one kind of mistake increases the other.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Choose and explain the error balance

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: A reading-help screener accepts more false positives. Why might that be reasonable?

choices.text: Missing a student who needs help is worse
Because false positives never have any cost at all for students, schools or teachers

questions.correct_answer: Missing a student who needs help is worse
questions.intro: Deciding the balance is a choice, not a technical fact. A school screening tool that flags students for extra reading help might accept more false positives (some students get help they did not need) to avoid false negatives (students who needed help and were missed). A tool that flags people for fraud investigations might need very few false positives, because a wrong flag harms an innocent person. Say which error you are trying to limit and why.

choices.text: Because false negatives do not exist
